item.title: Rules, London’s oldest restaurant, donated to National Trust
item.description: Historic eatery in capital’s theatreland given to heritage charity after changing hands only three times in 228 years When Thomas Rule served his first oyster to diners on Maiden Lane in London’s Covent Garden, “mad” George III was on the throne of England, John Adams was US president and William Pitt the Younger had just come up with a wheeze called income tax to pay for the Napoleonic wars. More than two centuries later, Rules , the restaurant Thomas founded in what became the capital’s theatreland, has outlasted nine British monarchs and 45 prime ministers – but has changed hands only… Fuente: The Guardian - World.

item.title: French MPs pass sweeping bill to combat sexual and gender-based violence
item.description: The National Assembly overwhelmingly passed the so-called “comprehensive” bill against sexist and sexual violence on Tuesday. The focus now shifts to the more conservative Senate, with the bill’s supporters fearing that its main advances could be watered down, even though the government insists it will act as guarantor of the bill’s ambition. Sponsored in the Assembly by eight political groups, from the Communists to Les Républicains (LR), the text was adopted by 503 votes to 0. Only the LFI (La France Insoumise) deputies abstained, denouncing in particular the removal of measures aimed at… Fuente: France 24 - English.

item.title: France's fed-up youth: Can presidential candidates connect with student movement?
item.description: Will it be autumn recess to the rescue for a beleaguered French government? Ministers no doubt counting the days until Friday evening when the holidays start in hopes that an unexpected student movement disappears as quickly as it materialized. A movement sparked three weeks ago by deteriorating conditions in a Paris area high school may take a leave of absence… but what about demands for a generation that feels left behind by cost cutting? Only one party’s sided vocally with the students since the very start, Jean-Luc Mélenchon’s far-left France Unbowed. Fuente: France 24 - English.

item.title: Albania police use tear gas on protesting students as stir turns violent
item.description: In Albania, student protests escalated into violent clashes with police in the capital, Tirana. These demonstrations aimed to highlight critical issues surrounding education and socio-economic challenges. Students raised urgent concerns over campus conditions, rising tuition fees, and uncertain job prospects. Deputy Prime Minister Albana Koçiu denounced the unrest, advocating for peaceful expression. This incident reflects a wider wave of student activism sweeping across Europe, demanding systemic change. Fuente: The Times of India - World.

item.title: In Brazil, thousands march fearing return of Bolsonaro presidency
item.description: Thousands of young Brazilians have taken to the streets to support President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva and voice fears of a return to power for the Bolsonaro political movement, amid a closely watched presidential race. Many protesters say they are worried about their future, particularly the impact a far-right government could have on universities and education. FRANCE 24’s Jan Onoszko reports from Brazil. Fuente: France 24 - English.

item.title: Elecciones anticipadas en España: ¿cómo se vota y en qué consiste el método D’Hondt?
item.description: España celebrará elecciones generales anticipadas el próximo 29 de noviembre para renovar el Congreso de los Diputados y el Senado. En este país, los ciudadanos no eligen directamente al presidente del Gobierno: votan a sus representantes parlamentarios, y son los diputados del Congreso quienes deciden mediante una votación quién puede encabezar el Ejecutivo. Para entender los resultados electorales, también es importante conocer el método D’Hondt, la fórmula que se utiliza para repartir los escaños del Congreso entre las candidaturas en cada circunscripción. Fuente: France 24 - Español.
item.dc:creator: Yurany Arciniegas Salamanca

item.title: 12 mil reproducciones · 137 reacciones | Eleições nos EUA - O empresário Elon Musk gastou cerca de US$ 366 milhões (R$ 1,8 bilhão) para apoiar o Partido Republicano, do presidente Donald Trump, no ciclo eleitoral das eleições de meio de mandato de 2026 nos Estados Unidos. Desse total, US$ 276 milhões (R$ 1,3 bilhão) foram doados desde julho. A informação foi divulgada inicialmente pelo jornal "The New York Times". Com isso, Musk se torna o maior o doador individual nas eleições deste ano, de acordo com os registros de financiamento de campanha. Esta é uma mudança drástica no posicionamento político do empresário. Em maio do ano passado, Musk disse que pretendia reduzir seus gastos políticos. “Acho que já fiz o suficiente”, disse ele na época. A iniciativa de Musk é interpretada por veículos da imprensa internacional como uma ofensiva contra democratas do Congresso americano, que pedem investigações sobre seus contratos com o governo como CEO da empresa aeroespacial SpaceX. Também há pedidos sobre sua atuação à frente do Departamento de Eficiência Governamental no governo Trump. Musk teve um desentendimento com Trump ao deixar seu cargo no governo, mas os dois se reconciliaram. Trump concedeu a Musk a Medalha Nacional de Ciência na semana passada. O empresário também voltou ao governo, agora como conselheiro de um estudo sobre o futuro da guerra. Saiba mais no #g1 #trump #musk #eua | g1 - O Portal de Notícias da globo

item.description: A pocos días de la segunda vuelta presidencial en Brasil, los candidatos intensifican sus gestos hacia el electorado católico durante las celebraciones de Nuestra Señora de Aparecida, patrona del país. Flávio Bolsonaro volvió a rechazar los rumores que lo vinculaban con una supuesta intención de retirar a la Virgen su condición de patrona. Durante la jornada, el senador visitó a su padre, Jair Bolsonaro, y agradeció a Dios, mientras que el presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva participó en una misa y criticó la suspensión de su canal de difusión en WhatsApp por presuntas publicaciones de… Fuente: France 24 - Español.
